overall: The AG found no Open Meeting Law violation: the Council's October 6, 2022 team-building training was not a meeting because members did not deliberate, so no notice or minutes were required.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the Council attended and deliberated at an October 6, 2022 training session that was not properly noticed to the public.
allegations.key_passage: we find that the Council did not deliberate during the training session as any discussions that occurred during the training related to purely interpersonal dynamics and did not involve the Council’s exercise of governmental business, policy, or administration.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the Council failed to post notice of the October 6, 2022 training session, which a quorum attended.
allegations.key_passage: Because there was no deliberation among Council members, the training fell within one of the exceptions to the definition of “meeting” for purposes of the Open Meeting Law.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the Council held a meeting on October 6, 2022 for which no minutes were created.
allegations.key_passage: Accordingly, the Council was not required to comply with the Law’s requirements to post notice or create minutes.

note: Read by a language model from the letter; every key passage is checked verbatim against it and dropped if not. A holding is the Attorney General’s reading of the law in this case only.
